- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp spike in model forecast (e.g., >50% above recent mean), true outcome typically corrects downward; apply “overshoot correction” by subtracting 20–40% of spike magnitude.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating positive/negative swings, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply “sentiment decay” — reduce forecast weight by 30% for sentiment changes >0.50 in magnitude.  
- If true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), model may be overconfident; apply “lag correction” — shift forecast down by 0.1–0.3 units per day for next 3 days.
